description: Hand-curated, domain-agnostic exemplar test cases shipped with TestForge for few-shot prompt injection on fresh deployments. Each is a full TC stored in test_cases (flagged is_seeded=1) with a matching reference in exemplar_test_cases.

exemplars.title: User signs in with valid credentials

description.objective: Verify that a registered user can sign in with valid credentials and reach the authenticated landing page.
assumptions: User account exists and is active

preconditions: Test user 'qa.user@example.com' exists with status Active
No active session exists for the test user (cleared cookies or incognito)
environment: Application reachable at the test environment base URL

steps.step: Navigate to the application sign-in page
steps.expectedResult: Sign-in form is displayed with Username and Password fields and a Sign In button

steps.step: Enter valid username and password and click Sign In
steps.expectedResult: User is redirected to the authenticated landing page within 5 seconds

steps.step: Confirm authenticated state
steps.expectedResult: User's display name appears in the page header; a session cookie is present in browser storage

exemplars.title: User creates a new record and verifies it persists

description.objective: Verify that a user can create a new record through the standard creation form, the record persists, and is retrievable after navigation.
scope: Single-record create flow with persistence verification
assumptions: User has Create permission for the record type
Creation endpoint accepts the schema defined for the record type

preconditions: User is signed in with Create permission for the target record type
No existing record matches the test name
Test environment data store is reachable
environment: Application reachable at the test environment base URL
testData: Valid values for all required fields per the record schema

steps.step: Navigate to the record list view
steps.expectedResult: List view displays without errors; 'Create New' action is visible and enabled

steps.step: Click 'Create New'
steps.expectedResult: Creation form opens with all required fields shown and marked as required

steps.step: Fill all required fields with valid data and click Save
steps.expectedResult: Form submits without validation errors; confirmation 'Record created' is displayed; user returns to the list view

steps.step: Locate the new record in the list view
steps.expectedResult: Record with the test name is visible in the list with creation timestamp within the last 10 seconds

steps.step: Refresh the page
steps.expectedResult: Record with the test name is still present in the list, confirming persistence

steps.step: Delete the test record via the row delete action
steps.expectedResult: Record is removed from the list view; confirmation 'Record deleted' is displayed

exemplars.title: API rejects malformed request body with specific error and no partial state change

description.objective: Verify that the API returns a structured error response when the request body fails validation, and that no record is created or modified in the database.
assumptions: Endpoint requires authentication and accepts JSON request bodies
Validation rules for the endpoint are documented

preconditions: Valid API token for a user with permission to call the endpoint
Pre-test row count for the target table is recorded
environment: API base URL reachable from test environment
Network logging available to capture request/response
equipment: API client capable of sending raw JSON (curl, Postman, or equivalent)
testData: Malformed body: required field 'name' omitted; field 'priority' set to a non-numeric value

steps.step: Record the current row count for the target database table
steps.expectedResult: Row count is captured for post-test comparison

steps.step: Send POST to the endpoint with the malformed body and valid auth token
steps.expectedResult: Server returns within 5 seconds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request)

steps.step: Inspect the response body
steps.expectedResult: Response body is JSON with fields 'error' (string) and 'details' (array); 'details' contains at least one entry referencing the omitted 'name' field and one referencing the invalid 'priority' value

steps.step: Verify the row count for the target table is unchanged
steps.expectedResult: Row count matches the pre-test value, confirming no partial state mutation

steps.step: Verify no audit log entry was created for a successful creation
steps.expectedResult: Audit log contains no 'created' event for the test user within the test time window

exemplars.title: Unauthorized user is denied access to a restricted resource and the attempt is logged

description.objective: Verify that a user without the required role is denied access to a restricted resource, receives an appropriate error response, and the denial event is captured in the audit log.
scope: Role-based access control on a specific resource
assumptions: Resource is protected by a role check
Audit logging is enabled for access denials

preconditions: Test user 'qa.user@example.com' exists with role 'QA Engineer' (not 'Admin')
Restricted resource is configured to require role 'Admin'
Audit log is queryable for the test time window
environment: Database access available for audit log verification

steps.step: Sign in as the test user (non-Admin role)
steps.expectedResult: Sign-in succeeds; user reaches the authenticated landing page

steps.step: Attempt to navigate to the restricted resource URL
steps.expectedResult: Navigation is intercepted; user is shown a 403 / 'Access Denied' page (not a generic 404)

steps.step: Verify the response status code or page indicator
steps.expectedResult: HTTP response status is 403, OR the page displays the standard 'Access Denied' template with a request ID

steps.step: Query the audit log for the test user within the test time window
steps.expectedResult: Audit log contains one 'ACCESS_DENIED' entry with the test user's ID, the restricted resource path, and a timestamp within the last minute

steps.step: Sign out
steps.expectedResult: Session is terminated; subsequent navigation to any authenticated route returns the sign-in page

exemplars.title: Numeric input field enforces minimum and maximum bounds at edges

description.objective: Verify that a numeric input field accepts values at the documented minimum and maximum, and rejects values outside the range with appropriate error feedback.
scope: Single numeric input field with documented min and max
assumptions: Field min is 1 and max is 100 per this exemplar (substitute actual values when applied)

preconditions: User is signed in with permission to use the form containing the numeric field
Form is in its initial empty state
testData: Boundary values: 0 (one below min), 1 (at min), 100 (at max), 101 (one above max)

steps.step: Enter value 0 (one below minimum) and attempt to submit the form
steps.expectedResult: Form does not submit; field-level error 'Value must be between 1 and 100' is displayed adjacent to the field

steps.step: Clear the field, enter value 1 (at minimum), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form submits successfully; no validation error is shown for this field

steps.step: Return to the form, clear the field, enter value 100 (at maximum), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form submits successfully; no validation error is shown for this field

steps.step: Return to the form, clear the field, enter value 101 (one above maximum), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form does not submit; the same field-level error is displayed

steps.step: Clear the form to restore the initial state
steps.expectedResult: Field is empty; no error messages remain visible

exemplars.title: Text field enforces minimum and maximum character length at all boundaries with proper error handling

description.objective: Verify that a text input field enforces both minimum and maximum character length at the boundary values, displays the correct error messages, handles whitespace-only input, and prevents typing past the maximum on both the client and server.
scope: Text input field with documented min and max length
assumptions: Min length is 3 characters and max length is 50 characters per this exemplar

preconditions: User is signed in with form access
Form is opened in a clean state with the field empty
environment: Network logging available to confirm server-side rejection

steps.step: Enter a 2-character value (below minimum) and attempt to submit
steps.expectedResult: Form rejects submission; error 'Must be at least 3 characters' is shown below the field

steps.step: Clear the field, enter a 3-character value (at minimum), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form accepts the input; no length error shown; submission succeeds

steps.step: Return to a clean form, enter a 50-character value (at maximum), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form accepts the input; no length error shown; submission succeeds

steps.step: Return to a clean form and attempt to type 51 characters into the field
steps.expectedResult: Field accepts only the first 50 characters; the 51st keystroke is ignored; if a character counter is present it shows '50/50'

steps.step: Attempt to paste a 51-character value into the field
steps.expectedResult: Field truncates pasted content to 50 characters OR displays error 'Maximum length is 50 characters' — behavior matches documented design

steps.step: Clear the field, enter 5 space characters (whitespace-only within valid length), and submit
steps.expectedResult: Form rejects with 'Field cannot be only whitespace' if trim validation is documented; otherwise document the actual behavior as a separate finding

steps.step: Bypass client-side validation (direct API call) and send a 51-character value to the server
steps.expectedResult: Server returns HTTP 400 with an error indicating length violation; no record is created in the data store

steps.step: Verify no record was persisted from the API-level rejection
steps.expectedResult: Data store row count for the test user is unchanged from the pre-test baseline

steps.step: Clear the form to restore the initial state
steps.expectedResult: Field is empty; no error messages or character-count warnings remain visible

exemplars.title: System handles empty input collection gracefully and returns expected empty-state response

description.objective: Verify that a feature accepting a collection of items handles an empty collection without errors, and that the response or UI clearly communicates the empty state rather than appearing broken.
scope: Endpoint or UI feature that processes a list of items
assumptions: The feature documents that an empty collection is a valid input
Documented behavior for empty selection is known (button disabled vs. enabled with guard)

preconditions: User is signed in with access to the feature
No items selected for the operation
testData: Empty list / empty selection / no items checked

steps.step: Open the feature view in its initial state with no items selected
steps.expectedResult: Feature view displays; the action button for the bulk operation is visible and its state matches the documented behavior (disabled OR enabled with a clear indicator)

steps.step: If the action button is enabled, trigger the operation with no items selected
steps.expectedResult: System does not throw an error; user is shown a clear empty-state message such as 'No items selected — choose at least one item to continue'; no state change occurs

steps.step: If the operation is an API call, inspect the response
steps.expectedResult: Response status is 200 with a structured empty result (e.g., {items: [], count: 0}) OR 400 with a validation message — matches documented behavior, not an unhandled 500

steps.step: Verify no audit log entry was written for a state change
steps.expectedResult: Audit log contains no entry for the test user attributable to this operation in the test time window

steps.step: Confirm the UI returns to a usable state
steps.expectedResult: No frozen spinners, no stack traces, no orphaned modals; user can navigate away or retry

exemplars.title: Concurrent updates to a shared record resolve deterministically without data corruption

description.objective: Verify that when two users update the same record simultaneously, the system applies a deterministic conflict-resolution strategy (last-write-wins, optimistic locking, or merge) and no data is silently lost or corrupted.
scope: Single shared record under concurrent edit
assumptions: Record has at least two editable fields

preconditions: Two distinct user accounts (User A and User B) both have edit permission on the test record
Test record exists with known initial field values: field1='initial-A', field2='initial-B'
Both users can open the record edit form simultaneously
environment: Two browser sessions or two API clients capable of issuing simultaneous requests
Database access for verifying final state

steps.step: User A opens the record for editing
steps.expectedResult: Edit form displays with field1='initial-A' and field2='initial-B'; a version token or timestamp is captured in form state

steps.step: User B opens the same record for editing before User A has saved
steps.expectedResult: Edit form displays the same initial values; User B's session captures the same version token

steps.step: User A sets field1='updated-by-A' and saves
steps.expectedResult: User A's save succeeds; record version increments; database reflects field1='updated-by-A', field2='initial-B'

steps.step: User B sets field2='updated-by-B' and attempts to save with the stale version token
steps.expectedResult: Response matches the documented strategy: optimistic lock returns 409 Conflict with 'record was modified'; last-write-wins accepts the save; merge produces a combined record

steps.step: Inspect the final database row state
steps.expectedResult: Final state matches the documented strategy (optimistic lock: field2 remains 'initial-B'; LWW: field2='updated-by-B' and field1 may revert; merge: both updates applied)

steps.step: If a conflict response was returned to User B, verify the response includes the current server-side values
steps.expectedResult: Response body contains the current record state so User B can resolve the conflict and retry

steps.step: Verify the audit log contains separate entries for User A's save and User B's attempt
steps.expectedResult: Audit log has two entries with distinct timestamps, user IDs, and outcome statuses (success/conflict)

steps.step: If User B retries with the latest version token and the original field2 update, verify the retry succeeds
steps.expectedResult: Second save succeeds; final record reflects both User A's field1 update and User B's field2 update

steps.step: Restore the record to its original state (field1='initial-A', field2='initial-B')
steps.expectedResult: Record is reset; both users' sessions can re-run the test from a clean state
